$schema_note: The ONE list of FRED series the site pulls every weekday (scripts/fetch-rates.mjs → the `rates` table) and reads back (lib/live-rates.ts → the rates strip on /tools and /market, and the seeds that pre-fill a calculator field). Both sides import this file, so the cron and the page cannot disagree about what a series is. `id` is the key in the `rates` table; `fred` is the FRED series it is fetched from where that differs (a `_YOY` id stores FRED's own percent-change-from-a-year-ago transform, `units: pc1`, so an index never reaches the page as a level). `unit` says what the stored figure is: `pct` a rate (shown 4.94%, moves in bps), `spread` a spread quoted in percent points (shown as bps), `pts` a share or a change (shown 2.9%, moves in points), `count` thousands of units at an annual rate (moves in percent). `freshDays` is one full publication cycle plus its release lag plus margin — see lib/live-rates.ts for why it is per series. `contractRate` is the standing fact that a loan document names this rate; whether a card currently takes it is the page's own list. Every entry here was verified from the runner: a series is added only once a dry run of the rates workflow has printed its FRED title and a current observation. `metroSeries` files the same shape under a covered metro (`metro` is the id in data/research/metros.json, or in data/data-metros.json for a metro area the site reads without a brief — the same series, the same readers, no brief behind them; `metric` one of unemployment / jobs_yoy / permits / hpi_yoy / rent_cpi_yoy; `area` what FRED's own title calls the place, short); `metroAliases` names, for a metro FRED publishes little for, the MSA whose figures fill the metrics it lacks — shown as the MSA's, never as the county's. `regionSeries` files the same shape under a Census region (`metro` is the region's id — northeast / midwest / south / west — never a covered metro's) for what the Housing Vacancy Survey publishes at no finer grain, and `metroRegions` names each covered metro's region, so every metro borrows its region's rental vacancy and the tile names the region. A metro's house price index is the FHFA division series where FRED carries one; Washington's and Atlanta's stopped at 2024 Q4 under the new delineations and are left out rather than shown stale. `source: bls` marks a series pulled from the BLS's own API rather than FRED — the CPI rent index for the areas the BLS redrew in 2018 (Washington, Baltimore, Los Angeles, San Francisco), which FRED does not carry; such a series is stored under its BLS id as the level, with `derived: yoy`, and never carries a FRED transform. The other metros' rent index is FRED's copy under the BLS's pre-2018 area code (A101 New York and so on), stored the same way so the two read alike. `source: census` marks a series read out of the Census Bureau's own Housing Vacancy Survey workbook (scripts/fetch-hvs.mjs, quarterly): the rental vacancy rate for one of the 75 largest metro areas, stored under an id of ours (`HVS_RVR_<cbsa>`) with the survey's margin of error in a companion series named by `moe`, and matched in the workbook by the metro area's name — `census` is the prefix of that name, kept short of where the two tables' spellings diverge. The dry run prints the row each metro matched, so a wrong name is visible rather than silently another city.
